sources.rationale: Binds to extracted route records: parameters captured by path()/re_path() patterns arrive as handler arguments chosen by the requester. The request object itself is a handler parameter and rides handler-parameter seeding, not a module attribute.
Constructing a QueryDict parses raw attacker bytes (the request.body idiom for non-form methods); the result is attacker-chosen.

sinks.rationale: RawSQL embeds its first argument into the query as written; the params argument is the only parameterised channel.
Manager.raw(sql) executes the given SQL text. Name-equality match on a common method name, hence heuristic confidence with the manager-receiver hint.
QuerySet.extra() splices the where/select/tables fragments into the generated SQL verbatim — Django's own docs mark it a last-resort injection surface.
Redirecting to an attacker-chosen absolute URL is an open redirect.
